newsitem.title: USA: Sinatra remains in hospital after heart attack.
newsitem.headline: Sinatra remains in hospital after heart attack.

text.p: Frank Sinatra remained in the hospital on Monday continuing his recovery from a mild heart attack and there was no word on when he might be released.
"There is no change in his condition and the prognosis continues to be good," Sinatra's spokeswoman, Susan Reynolds, said.

The 81-year-old singer and movie star was staying in a private room at Cedars-Sinai Medical Centre, where he was admitted last Thursday after suffering what his doctors called an "uncomplicated heart attack."
Reynolds said it was not known when Sinatra would be allowed to return home. His wife, Barbara, his children and other relatives have been regular visitors at his bedside.

Soon after Sinatra entered the hospital, NBC News cited unnamed sources saying he was suffering from Alzheimer's disease, a degenerative brain disorder. But Reynolds and Sinatra's family members have steadfastly denied the report.
Sinatra was rushed to Cedars-Sinai only two days after being released from the hospital, where he spent last Monday night for an undisclosed complaint.

In November, he spent eight days at the same hospital after being admitted for what was described as a pinched nerve. He later developed pneumonia and was also reported to have suffered a minor heart attack at the time.
